by.claim: rfc-001-sync-impersonation.md's design only impersonates the sync operation (the destination service account performs the actual apply), leaving diff/dry-run untouched by impersonation config; this produces both T-26271's in-cluster CLI diff failure (server-side diff dry-run is authorized by Kubernetes as a patch, and the impersonated destination SA lacks that patch on cluster-scoped resources like ClusterRole/cert-manager-cainjector) and T-28695's external-cluster problem (Server-Side Diff in the application-controller reconcile path ignores destinationServiceAccounts entirely and runs as the raw, deliberately least-privilege cluster-secret credential, forcing ever-broadening unbounded patch RBAC grants).

prd-progressive-sync-deletion.md's Reverse deletion strategy is designed to wait for one Application to be fully deleted before moving to the next step; T-28511 shows that when a matched Application is stuck in Progressing (deletion never completes) and is deleted manually, the applicationset-controller does not respect its Deleting status and restarts the wave from the top, producing the infinite delete/recreate loop the PRD's sequential-wait design does not account for.
